title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The UK government has responded to the Committee's 2020 report on Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards by outlining new measures to ensure AI systems are safe, transparent, and fair. It plans to update regulatory frameworks, support research and development, and collaborate with industry to promote responsible AI usage across public services.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: Ofqual has released a policy outlining how it will oversee and manage the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector, aiming to maintain the fairness, reliability, and security of exams and assessments. The approach seeks to set clear rules for AI deployment, monitor its impact on testing standards, and ensure that any AI tools used are transparent and do not compromise the integrity of qualifications.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: The report examines how copyrighted works are used to train AI systems and evaluates the legal, economic, and social impacts of that practice. It provides recommendations for balancing creators’ rights with the need for data to advance AI technology.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The UK government has responded to the House of Lords Select Committee’s report “AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency” by outlining a plan to strengthen AI safety, boost innovation, and protect jobs while ensuring ethical use of technology. It promises tighter regulation, increased investment in research and skills development, and collaboration with industry to build trust and competitiveness in the global AI landscape.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: The document sets out the purpose, scope, and responsibilities of a committee tasked with reviewing how artificial intelligence affects public standards. It also includes FAQs that explain the review process, timelines, and key considerations for stakeholders.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: CSPL has written to the Science and Technology Committee to share its views on how artificial intelligence should be governed. The submission likely includes concerns and recommendations for AI policy and oversight.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: The policy explains how the growing use of AI in medical products will shape future regulatory frameworks, addressing new safety, efficacy and data‑quality standards. It also outlines how to apply the AI White Paper principles to promote transparency, accountability and patient protection in AI‑driven medical solutions.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: The Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy outlines a vision for the organisation to become the most effective, efficient, trusted, and influential AI‑driven defence body worldwide for its size. It aims to achieve this by developing advanced AI capabilities, fostering innovation, and maintaining the highest standards of security and ethical use.

title: Transport artificial intelligence action plan
description: Sets out how DfT will work with the transport sector to exploit the opportunities from AI while managing potential risks.
summary: The Transport Artificial Intelligence Action Plan explains how the Department for Transport will partner with the transport sector to harness the benefits of artificial intelligence. It also outlines measures to address and mitigate the potential risks associated with AI implementation.

title: Copyright and artificial intelligence: progress report
description: A progress report on the use of copyright works in the development of AI systems, under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act.
summary: This report examines how AI developers are using copyrighted materials to train and improve their models, and assesses compliance with the Data (Use and Access) Act’s Section 137. It highlights the current state of practice, identifies challenges, and offers recommendations for balancing innovation with copyright protection.
